## Question 1 (Projects)

a) What is the purpose of a Project in RStudio? {{< hp glyph="." >}}Why do I recommend creating a project rather than simply saving all your course stuff in a normal computer folder?

b) What are some benefits of having a consistent naming convention for the files in your project? {{< hp glyph="." >}}What kinds of tasks might be easier if you stick with a convention?

## Question 2 (Quarto and Markdown)

a) What is the difference between a .qmd file and a .html file created by Quarto? {{< hp glyph="." >}}When would you send the .qmd file to a collaborator and when would you send the .html file?

b) Quarto lets you include many code chunks in the same document. {{< hp glyph="." >}}When would you want to put all your code in a single chunk and when would you want to break it up across multiple chunks?

c) Use markdown headings to break your document into sections: one per question. Because Header level 1 is usually used for a document title, I recommend using Header level 2. (Please continue using markdown headings in your future assignments.)

## Question 3 (Assignment and Naming)

a) Why is it important to give your objects in R good names? {{< hp glyph="." >}}When might poorly thought-out names cause problems for a programmer?

b) Sam is designing a treehouse. The plan is basically a big rectangular box with a wall that is 5.32 ft wide and 4.74 ft long (Sam is very precise). Using R, calculate the area of the treehouse and save that value to an object named `area`. Then use that object to calculate the `volume` of the treehouse, assuming the walls are 5.61 ft tall. Print the `volume` object.

$$Area = Length \times Width$$

$$Volume = Area \times Height$$

c) Help me fix my code! "I want to assign a name to my extraversion score on the Five Factor Model personality test."


::: {.cell renv.ignore='true'}

```{.r .cell-code}
5FM_extraversion <- 23
## Error in parse(text = input): <text>:1:2: unexpected symbol
## 1: 5FM_extraversion
##      ^
```
:::


d) Help me fix my code! "I want to calculate the average of three objects corresponding to negative emotion self-reports."


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
anger <- 3
sadness <- 4
fear <- 3
negative_emotion <- (anger + sadness + faer) / 3
## Error:
## ! object 'faer' not found
```
:::
